Hi Aiden —

Great to meet earlier today. Short recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum on the perf qualification side. I focused this note on the SLO / context-window constraints you surfaced during the call.

Quick summary of what we heard from your team:
- Target latency: 200 ms p95 for single-turn responses, 350 ms p95 for streaming-first-token latency.
- Throughput target: sustained 150 QPS for embedding + generation mix; burst to 400 QPS during peak sync windows.
- Concurrency: up to ~250 concurrent users that issue requests; typical per-user session has 1–3 concurrent requests.
- Context window: 6k tokens input (average 3.2k), 1k tokens max output. Some sessions include long system prompts + dense chat history.
- Streaming: important for UX on the mobile app; want first-token under 350 ms and steady stream at ~30–60 tokens/sec.

Implications we discussed:
- 6k input + 1k output materially increases KV cache and memory pressure on GPU; will affect per-request latency compared with 2k-window runs.
- Streaming first-token latency depends on CPU-to-GPU pipeline and batching; continuous batching is valuable but must be bounded to maintain p95s.
- Autoscaling should consider prefix-cache hit rates — we recommended prefix caching for commonly repeated system prompts to reduce token work.

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) StitchLabs: share a small representative prompt set (10–20 sessions) and one worst-case long session by Friday. Prefer anonymized examples. (Aiden)
2) Redwood: provision a 2-week perf PoC with a dedicated test harness (we'll provide the harness link) and a reserved slot for two benchmark runs. We'll configure:
   - model: rdx-large-v2 (quantized variant)
   - runtime config: bounded batching (max latency 120ms), prefix caching on, kv-cache memory profiling on
   - load: synthetic mix to replicate 150 QPS sustained + 400 QPS bursts
3) Exchange quick doc: our perf matrix + suggested sample rate limits and fallback (attached). (Marissa)
4) Align on success criteria: p95 <= 200ms for single-turn; streaming first-token <= 350ms and average streaming throughput >= 30 tokens/sec; no OOMs during 400 QPS bursts.

Attachments: redwood-perf-matrix-stitchlabs.xlsx (perf matrix), stitchlabs-poc-checklist.pdf (PoC logistics).

Can you confirm A) you'll share the sample prompts and B) two preferred 2-hour windows for the PoC runs next week?

Thanks —

For SLAs we look at the steady-state throughput per open stream (so your client-side buffer should target ~30 tokens/sec delivered from server). Aggregate throughput matters for capacity planning, but UX depends on per-stream rate.
>
> 2) Tail spikes during bursts — recommended fallbacks (in order):
>    - Immediate: switch to a lower-latency model variant (rdx-medium-v2) with reduced output quality (automated routing).
>    - Mid-term: enable prefix caching aggressively for repeated system prompts to cut prefix tokens.
>    - Defensive: circuit-breaker that rejects non-critical heavy requests (e.g., embeddings for non-urgent background jobs) with 429 + Retry-After.
>
> Tactical knobs for the PoC we will apply:
> - Bounded batching (max latency cap) so we avoid unbounded batching growth in peaks.
> - KV-cache warmup step to pre-populate common prefixes before the run.
> - Per-route concurrency caps and a fallback policy that routes to cheaper variants during sustained saturation.
